\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Output prefix encoding]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.outPrefix}
\label{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.outPrefix}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.descTail}
For a Boolean list $w$, define its output prefix to be the concatenation of two true
bits, the descriptor tail of $w$, and the two-bit list $(	ext{true},	ext{false})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time output-prefix construction]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.polyTimeComputable_outPrefix}
\label{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.polyTimeComputable_outPrefix}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.outPrefix, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_transduce}
\difficulty{1}
The function that maps a bit string $w$ to the output prefix formed from the description
tail of $w$ is computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time gate-clause generation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.polyTimeComputable_gateClauses}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time circuit satisfiability transformation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.polyTimeComputable_dagCktSatToSAT3}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{BoolCircuit.polyTimeComputable_dagCktSatToSAT3}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.dagCktSatToSAT3_eq, BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.polyTimeComputable_gateClauses, BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.polyTimeComputable_isValid, BoolCircuit.CktSatReduction.polyTimeComputable_outPrefix, BoolCircuit.dagCktSatToSAT3, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Std.Sat.CNF.serialize, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const}
\difficulty{5}
There exist a deterministic Turing machine with a finite state set and natural numbers
$C,c$ such that, on every finite bit string $w$, it halts within $C(|w|+1)^c$ steps and
outputs the following transformation: decode $w$ as a directed acyclic Boolean circuit;
if decoding succeeds and the circuit is well formed with every gate reading at most two
arguments, output the binary serialization of its Tseitin conjunctive normal form with
the output vertex required to be true; otherwise output the serialization of the CNF
consisting of one empty clause.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reduction to 3-CNF satisfiability]
\lean{BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_polyTimeReducible_SAT3}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_polyTimeReducible_SAT3}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang, BoolCircuit.dagCktSatToSAT3, BoolCircuit.mem_dagCktSatLang_iff_mem_SAT3, BoolCircuit.polyTimeComputable_dagCktSatToSAT3, Complexity.PolyTimeReducible, Complexity.SAT3}
\difficulty{1}
There is a polynomial-time computable function $f$ from Boolean strings to Boolean
strings such that, for every Boolean string $x$, $x$ encodes a satisfiable directed
acyclic Boolean circuit with at most two inputs per gate if and only if $f(x)$ encodes a
satisfiable CNF formula in which every clause has at most three literals.
\end{theorem}
